154	          if [[ -z "$ALL" ]]; then

258	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

274	      # Parses vitest's own JSON reporter output (test-results.json) and the
275	      # v8 coverage provider's json-summary (coverage/coverage-summary.json,
276	      # both produced by test:coverage's flags / vitest.config.ts's
277	      # coverage.reporter) into a single PR comment — pass/fail counts plus
278	      # a per-top-level-directory coverage breakdown. Upserts on an exact
279	      # HTML-comment marker so a redeploy updates the same comment instead
280	      # of spamming the thread, same pattern deploy-preview.yml's MRT
281	      # preview comment already uses. Runs even when the test step above
282	      # failed (always()) so a failing PR still gets the pass/fail count —
283	      # the coverage half of the comment degrades gracefully if the files
284	      # are missing (a hard crash before coverage was even written).
285	      - name: Post coverage/results summary to the PR
286	        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
287	        uses: actions/github-script@v7
288	        with:
289	          script: |
290	            const fs = require('fs')
291	
292	            const marker = '<!-- vitest-summary -->'
293	            let body = `${marker}\n## 🧪 Vitest Results\n\n`
294	
295	            let testResults = null
296	            try {
297	              testResults = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('test-results.json', 'utf8'))
298	            } catch (e) {
299	              body += `⚠️ Could not read test results (${e.message}) — the test run likely crashed before writing output.\n`
300	            }
301	
302	            if (testResults) {
303	              const { numTotalTests, numPassedTests, numFailedTests, numPendingTests, success } = testResults
304	              const icon = success ? '✅' : '❌'
305	              body += `${icon} **${numPassedTests}/${numTotalTests} passed**`
306	              if (numFailedTests) body += `, **${numFailedTests} failed**`
307	              if (numPendingTests) body += `, ${numPendingTests} skipped`
308	              body += '\n\n'
309	            }
310	
311	            let summary = null
312	            try {
313	              summary = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('coverage/coverage-summary.json', 'utf8'))
314	            } catch (e) {
315	              body += `_Coverage summary unavailable (${e.message})._\n`
316	            }
317	
318	            if (summary) {
319	              const total = summary.total
320	              body += `**Coverage — ${total.lines.pct}% lines** (${total.lines.covered}/${total.lines.total}), `
321	              body += `${total.branches.pct}% branches, ${total.functions.pct}% functions\n\n`
322	
323	              // Roll up per top-level directory under overrides/app/ — the
324	              // per-file table from the raw summary is too long to be a
325	              // useful PR comment; this is the same rollup grain the local
326	              // text reporter already prints.
327	              const dirs = {}
328	              for (const [filePath, data] of Object.entries(summary)) {
329	                if (filePath === 'total') continue
330	                const match = filePath.match(/overrides\/app\/([^/]+)\//)
331	                const dir = match ? match[1] : 'other'
332	                dirs[dir] ??= { total: 0, covered: 0 }
333	                dirs[dir].total += data.lines.total
334	                dirs[dir].covered += data.lines.covered
335	              }
336	
337	              body += '| Directory | Line coverage |\n|---|---|\n'
338	              for (const [dir, { total: t, covered: c }] of Object.entries(dirs).sort()) {
339	                const pct = t > 0 ? ((c / t) * 100).toFixed(1) : '100.0'
340	                body += `| \`app/${dir}\` | ${pct}% (${c}/${t}) |\n`
341	              }
342	              body += '\n<sub>Full HTML report: see the `vitest-coverage-report` artifact on this run.</sub>\n'
343	            }
344	
345	            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
346	              owner: context.repo.owner,
347	              repo: context.repo.repo,
348	              issue_number: context.issue.number,
349	              per_page: 100,
350	            })
351	            const existing = comments.find(
352	              (c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(marker) && c.user?.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
353	            )
354	            if (existing) {
355	              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
356	                owner: context.repo.owner,
357	                repo: context.repo.repo,
358	                comment_id: existing.id,
359	                body,
360	              })
361	            } else {
362	              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
363	                owner: context.repo.owner,
364	                repo: context.repo.repo,
365	                issue_number: context.issue.number,
366	                body,
367	              })
368	            }

3	# SFCC-751 develop-PR path, split out of qa.yml's e2e-browserstack
4	# (2026-08-25 cost review). Per-story Zephyr-linked BrowserStack execution
5	# against a develop-targeted PR's own ephemeral MRT preview
6	# (deploy-preview.yml), triggered the instant that preview finishes
7	# building instead of polling for it from an already-running, already-
8	# billed job. The old design started in parallel with Deploy Preview and
9	# slept in a loop waiting for it — up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner
10	# time per push. workflow_run fires exactly once, exactly when Deploy
11	# Preview completes, with everything this job needs already in the event
12	# payload or a downloadable artifact — no polling, so no billed wait.
13	#
14	# release/** PRs are unaffected — deploy-preview.yml never runs for
15	# fix/release-* branches, so this workflow never fires for them; they keep
16	# using qa.yml's e2e-browserstack (full suite, static test tier, no wait).
17	#
18	# GitHub only evaluates a workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition
19	# from the repository's default branch — this file is invisible to Actions
20	# entirely until merged to develop, and (like zephyr-results-sync.yml) can
21	# never be dry-run against a real PR pre-merge. See testing.md's note on
22	# zephyr-results-sync.yml for the same caveat.
23	on:
24	  workflow_run:
25	    workflows: ['Deploy Preview']
26	    types: [completed]
27	
28	permissions:
29	  contents: read
30	  actions: read # to download artifacts from the triggering Deploy Preview run and look up its matching QA run
31	  pull-requests: read # to find the open PR for this branch
32	
33	jobs:
34	  e2e-browserstack:
35	    name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)
36	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
37	    # A cancelled Deploy Preview run skips this job entirely (there's
38	    # nothing to test and no hostname artifact could exist). Any other
39	    # conclusion still runs -- if Deploy Preview failed rather than
40	    # succeeded, "Resolve BrowserStack test target" below fails the job
41	    # loudly instead of silently testing an unrelated environment (see
42	    # that step's own comment for why the old test-tier fallback was
43	    # removed, CodeRabbit, 2026-08-26).
44	    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'
45	    timeout-minutes: 25
46	    environment: test # for the E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_* secrets
47	    steps:
48	      # Checked out at the triggering run's own head_sha, not the default
49	      # branch — this job needs to execute the PR's own e2e specs and
50	      # scripts/computeBuildName.mjs, not develop's copy of them (unlike
51	      # zephyr-results-sync.yml, which deliberately checks out develop for
52	      # a script-trust reason that doesn't apply here — see that
53	      # workflow's comment). This carries the same secrets-exposure shape
54	      # qa.yml's old pull_request-triggered e2e-browserstack job already
55	      # had: real BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_* secrets alongside PR-branch code.
56	      # Acceptable under this repo's branch model (feature/fix branches
57	      # only, never a fork — see AGENTS.md > Branch Rules); would need
58	      # re-review if fork-based PRs are ever introduced.
59	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
60	        with:
61	          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
62	
63	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
64	        with:
65	          node-version: '24'
66	          cache: 'npm'
67	
68	      # --ignore-scripts, not --include=dev with lifecycle scripts enabled:
69	      # this job checks out and executes a PR branch's own code with real
70	      # BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_*/E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_* secrets in scope, and
71	      # workflow_run grants those secrets unconditionally -- unlike
72	      # pull_request, there is no pending-approval gate here even for a
73	      # same-repo branch. Without --ignore-scripts, anyone with push access
74	      # to a feature/fix branch could add a preinstall/postinstall script
75	      # to exfiltrate every secret this job can see, with no review step
76	      # in between (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-26). Skipping
77	      # lifecycle scripts is safe here: this job never builds or runs the
78	      # app locally (it only drives Playwright against an already-deployed
79	      # preview), so it doesn't need postinstall's translation-compilation
80	      # or registry-generation side effects.
81	      - name: Install dependencies
82	        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
83	
84	      # Single API call, no loop — by the time Deploy Preview has finished
85	      # (~5-10 min after push), the PR this branch belongs to has existed
86	      # for the whole run, so there's nothing to wait for here either.
87	      - name: Find open PR for this branch
88	        id: pr
89	        env:
90	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
91	          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
92	        run: |
93	          PR_JSON=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open \
94	            --json number,title,body,baseRefName --jq '.[0] // empty')
95	          if [[ -z "$PR_JSON" ]]; then

101	          if [[ "$BASE" != "develop" ]]; then
102	            # deploy-preview.yml only triggers on feature/**, fix/** pushes,
103	            # which per AGENTS.md > Branch Rules always target develop — this
104	            # is a defensive check, not an expected path.
105	            echo "PR #$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number') targets $BASE, not develop -- skipping."

110	          echo "number=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

112	          # attacker-controllable free text and could contain newlines or
113	          # break a later env: interpolation otherwise.

119	      # and self-contained, and this workflow has no other dependency on
120	      # qa.yml's run. No key found -> nothing to scope a per-story

134	      # detect-changes (qa.yml) finishes in well under a minute; Deploy
135	      # Preview takes several minutes minimum, so by the time this job
136	      # starts, that artifact is essentially guaranteed to already exist.
137	      # If the lookup or download comes up empty for any reason, fail open

153	        if: steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id != ''

155	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
156	        with:
157	          name: e2e-scope
158	          run-id: ${{ steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id }}
159	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
160	
161	      - name: Check e2e relevance
162	        id: relevance
163	        if: steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''
164	        run: |
165	          if [[ -f e2e-scope.json ]] && [[ "$(jq -r '.e2e' e2e-scope.json)" == "false" ]]; then
166	            echo "Nothing e2e-relevant changed on this commit (per qa.yml's detect-changes) -- skipping BrowserStack."
167	            echo "relevant=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
168	          else
169	            echo "relevant=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
170	          fi
171

173	        id: build-name
174	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
175	        run: |
176	          PRIMARY_KEY=$(echo "${{ steps.jira.outputs.keys }}" | awk '{print $1}')
177	          NAME=$(node scripts/computeBuildName.mjs "$PRIMARY_KEY")
178	          echo "name=$NAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

183

185	      # -- see that workflow's own comment for the drift reason.

28	    # elsewhere (e.g. unit-tests, or the develop-PR path's own PR/Jira-key
29	    # lookup) may still have a real BrowserStack build worth syncing. The
30	    # sync script itself no-ops cleanly if no build exists for this run

36	      # workflow_run jobs get real secrets regardless of who triggered the
37	      # original run — checking out and then executing a PR branch's own
38	      # version of scripts/*.mjs at that ref would let a modified script on
39	      # the branch exfiltrate BROWSERSTACK_*/ZEPHYR_*/JIRA_* directly
40	      # (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-25). No ref: means the
41	      # default branch, which is also the only ref GitHub ever evaluates a
42	      # workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition from — this job
43	      # could never have run against a PR branch's version of itself

52	      # e2e-browserstack job computed — not recompute it. This job checks

- **No `schedule:` / cron.** None anywhere in the file.
- **No `workflow_dispatch:`** → **cannot be dispatched manually. NO.**
- **No `workflow_call:`** (not reusable).
